title: HC Sean Payton on the challenge of facing Jacksonville’s defense: 'It’s a really talented front 7’
headline: Payton says Marvin Mims Jr. is set to return punts and kickoffs, but his status for Sunday vs. Jacksonville remains unclear.
summary: Payton said the Broncos are using a recovery-focused schedule after Monday night games, with a Saturday practice that is heavier than normal. He described Jacksonville's defense as well coached and purposeful, especially in generating takeaways from zone coverage and disrupting the ball. He called their front seven very talented and said stopping the run gives any team a balanced foundation. On offense, he said the Broncos need patience against Jacksonville's zones, with ball security required at the catch point. Payton said the Week 1 loss did not go the way anyone wanted and took responsibility for it, and he said Bo Nix's tape review involved many players who felt the same way. On Marvin Mims Jr., Payton said he will return punts and kickoffs, though kickoff usage varies by game plan. When asked whether Mims could miss Sunday, Payton did not give a clear answer. He also said the team is only at the start of its preparation, with the first practice held that day.

injuries.detail: Asked if he is in jeopardy of missing Sunday's game; Payton did not give a clear answer and deflected to the calendar. Mims was hurt later in the prior game.

signals.note: A confirmed return role adds expected opportunities for return-yardage production, though kickoff usage can change by game plan.

title: Matt LaFleur: MarShawn Lloyd has 'shown a lot of confidence that he is able to do it'
headline: LaFleur expressed confidence in MarShawn Lloyd's workload, while Lukas Van Ness and Javon Hargrave are in the concussion protocol.
summary: LaFleur said Lukas Van Ness entered the concussion protocol Monday and Javon Hargrave yesterday, and that the effects appeared to be residual from an earlier incident. He stressed that the long-term outlook is unknown with concussions, which is why the protocol exists. On the offensive side, he said internal interior pressure makes it hard for a quarterback to stay in a clean pocket, and that more multi-tight-end personnel forces more preparation. He said Aaron Banks had a good day at work on Wednesday and hopes he can build on it, and he acknowledged that interior linemen have been in and out of the lineup over the past couple of years. He praised MarShawn Lloyd's toughness after the Week 1 game, saying Lloyd handled the hits he took and has shown a lot of confidence that he can handle a heavy load, which gives LaFleur confidence in him. LaFleur also praised Matthew Golden's downfield blocking on a long play, saying the team wants those blocks because they turn explosive plays into touchdowns. On the red zone, he said staying on schedule is the key, since tighter coverage and less field make throwing harder. He said that if Van Ness can't play, one of two backup defensive linemen who had strong camps should be ready to step in.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Sept. 17)
headline: Nick Herbig is being used both on the line and off the ball, a usage pattern McCarthy praised and expects to continue; Troy Fautanu has a limited plan and Joey (name unverified) is still working through a conditioning issue.
summary: McCarthy said the unnamed player referred to as Joey had a good day Wednesday, completed everything scheduled, and has a plan that he is working through, with more work expected Thursday. The injury report lists conditioning, and McCarthy declined to discuss his back, so the back is not confirmed as cleared. He called the ramp-up of that player a case-by-case process and did not commit to a timeline. McCarthy said Troy Fautanu is on a limited plan for Thursday and hopes he can get through practice. He said Max Iheanachor is improving but needs more reps, and that Thursday is a big day for him after missing a lot of padded work. He praised Nick Herbig as a dynamic playmaker, citing how the team is using him on the ball, off the ball, and in space to create targeting problems for the offense. On T.J. Watt, he said Watt's respect in the locker room is well earned and that he gave a strong pregame speech. Asked about Payton Wilson and speed at middle linebacker, McCarthy said the defense gives flexibility in schemes and personnel groups, so the focus is on how each week's game plan fits the players.
